reconcile.note: The Geneva Bible resolves the numbers by reading Ahaziah's forty-two as a co-regency date, crowned during his father's reign at twenty-two and confirmed later at forty-two.

discrepancy.note: Spinoza dismisses the co-regency harmonization of the forty-two figure as commentators inventing a meaning the plain Hebrew text does not state.

quotes.text: when it is said in 2 Chronicles, that Ahab was forty-two years old when he began to reign, they pretend that these years are computed from the reign of Omri, not from the birth of Ahab.
quotes.attr: Benedict de Spinoza (d. 1677), A Theologico-Political Treatise, Part II (1883 Elwes transl.), ch. IX, on 2 Chronicles 22:2.

sides.snippet: Twenty-two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign
sides.verseText: Twenty-two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri king of Israel.

sides.snippet: Forty-two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign
sides.verseText: Forty-two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
